products.name: Annex H — Signal
products.purpose: Explains the signal support for the operation and connects it to the base order.
products.owner: S6/G6 develops staff input; coordinate tasks through the operations staff and command approval process.
products.users: Commander, staff, subordinate S6s and supporting Signal units use it to understand responsibilities and support.
products.when: Prepare during planning; update when the order or support concept changes.
contents: reporting references. Confirm the prescribed format.
products.example: Compare a fictional staff collaboration requirement with the support concept: is an owner assigned for delivering and testing the service?
products.pitfall: Do not bury essential tasking in an annex without coordinating the base order. An annex is not a device configuration.

products.name: SOI — Signal Operating Instructions
products.purpose: Instructions for coordinating communications within a command.
products.owner: Authorized Signal personnel maintain and distribute the applicable instructions under higher-headquarters guidance.
products.users: Operators and supported staff use the authorized edition for consistent communications procedures.
products.when: Before an event and whenever the authorized edition or instructions change.
products.example: In a fictional exercise, check whether all training participants were briefed on the same approved edition.
products.pitfall: This lesson describes purpose only. It does not display or generate frequencies, call signs, authentication data or COMSEC.

products.name: Signal running estimate
products.purpose: A continuing assessment of whether current and future operations can be supported.
products.owner: S6/G6 synthesizes inputs from staff, supported users and Signal units.
products.users: Commander and planners use conclusions, recommendations and risk to make decisions.
products.when: Maintain continuously; update when facts, assumptions or supportability change, not just before a briefing.
products.example: A fictional service has not passed its acceptance check. Recommend a rehearsal or fallback and explain the consequence for the planned user task.
products.pitfall: An equipment percentage or red/amber/green slide alone does not explain what the commander should do.
products.locator: Refocusing Running Estimates; Refocusing Staff Tools

products.name: Network diagrams supporting Annex H
products.purpose: A visual explanation of the planned relationships and dependencies supporting communications.
products.owner: S6/G6 and network planners coordinate with supporting teams and service owners.
products.users: Staff use an overview to understand support; technicians use separately authorized detail for implementation.
products.when: Review during planning, before rehearsal and after an approved change.
products.example: Trace a dummy training user task from the user to a shared application and its supporting services. Ask what evidence proves the task works.
products.pitfall: A line on a diagram is not proof of interoperability. Exact appendix/tab placement and technical interfaces require applicable doctrine and approved documentation.

products.name: PACE communications plan
products.purpose: Identifies primary, alternate, contingency and emergency ways to meet a communication need.
products.owner: Warfighting-function leads develop their needs with S6/G6 advice and available support.
products.users: Users and operators need to understand the intended method and transition triggers.
products.when: Plan by user need and phase; rehearse before use and reassess after changes.
products.example: If a training chat service and its supposed alternate share the same unavailable transport, question whether the alternate is independent.
products.pitfall: Four application names are not four independent paths. S6/G6 supports the functional lead rather than inventing every staff workflow.

products.name: Signal synchronization matrix / support timeline
products.purpose: An editorial worksheet aligning support actions with the events they must enable.
products.owner: Staff planners, Signal company leaders and team chiefs coordinate dependencies and deadlines.
products.users: Supported staff and delivery teams use it to see who must finish what before the next event.
products.when: Build during planning; revise when event timing or support tasks change.
products.example: Place a dummy service rehearsal before the training briefing it must support. Identify who resolves a missed prerequisite.
products.pitfall: A tidy timeline is not evidence of completed coordination. This is a teaching aid, not a prescribed universal matrix.
products.locator: Network and PACE coordination with G6s

products.name: Signal requirements and support-request worksheet
products.purpose: Captures the user outcome and coordination needed before choosing a support solution.
products.owner: Supported user describes the task; S6/G6 validates needs with the supporting Signal organization.
products.users: Planners and Signal units use agreed requirements to scope support and identify gaps.
products.when: Start at mission receipt; revisit assumptions before committing resources.
products.example: Replace “need internet” with “authorized training staff must share and retrieve a dummy planning update.”
products.pitfall: A request is not an approval or a resource allocation. Local request formats and lead times must be confirmed.

products.name: Communications status report / Signal COP
products.purpose: A shared status view that explains communications availability and user impact.
products.owner: Operators report evidence; the designated staff or network-operations owner maintains the consolidated view.
products.users: S6/G6 and commanders use it to prioritize restoration and understand limits.
products.when: Update at required reporting points and when a significant change occurs.
products.example: Report “dummy shared workspace unavailable; local client opens; service-owner check pending” rather than “network red.”
products.pitfall: Status colors need definitions, time and evidence. This editorial view is not a replacement for the unit reporting SOP.
products.locator: Chapter 18: network reporting requirements and staff assessment context

products.name: Communications rehearsal plan and results
products.purpose: Organizes tests so users demonstrate the required communications before the event.
products.owner: S6/G6 coordinates with staff users, application owners and supporting teams.
products.users: Operators and staff verify function and understand fallback transitions.
products.when: Schedule after prerequisites are ready and before the supported event.
products.example: Two authorized training users exchange a dummy update; confirm receipt, correct view and the agreed fallback behavior.
products.pitfall: A ping or radio check alone does not prove the application workflow works. Record observed results instead of a blanket “all green.”

products.name: Site reconnaissance and readiness checklist
products.purpose: An editorial checklist for confirming that a proposed training setup can be supported.
products.owner: Signal team leaders coordinate with the supported staff, facilities, safety and logistics owners.
products.users: Company/platoon leaders use it to surface prerequisites before equipment arrives.
products.when: During coordination and reconnaissance; recheck before occupying the training site.
products.example: The training site has no confirmed power support. Identify the responsible coordinator before promising service availability.
products.pitfall: This is not an engineering, electrical-safety or siting authorization. No real site locations or operational layout belong in this app.
products.locator: Expeditionary preparation, environment and transport lessons

products.name: Signal task organization and support responsibilities
products.purpose: An editorial role map showing who provides, receives and coordinates support.
products.owner: Operations staff and commanders establish relationships; Signal planners explain the support implications.
products.users: S6/G6, Signal company leaders and team chiefs use the agreed responsibilities to avoid gaps.
products.when: Coordinate during planning and review whenever teams or supported requirements change.
products.example: A training help request reaches an operator but nobody owns the application. Assign the missing coordination role.
products.pitfall: A diagram does not create command authority or change a support relationship. Actual responsibilities follow orders and policy.

products.name: Service acceptance and shift handover record
products.purpose: An editorial record of what works, what remains unresolved and who is taking responsibility.
products.owner: Outgoing and incoming operators coordinate with service owners and the supported user.
products.users: Teams use it to continue support without losing evidence or unfinished actions.
products.when: At service handoff, shift change and recovery verification.
products.example: An incoming training operator finds a service marked available but no user-task test. Request verification and retain the limitation.
products.pitfall: A signed checklist does not certify interoperability. Keep actual credentials and configuration records in authorized systems.

products.name: Signal SOP / TACSOP contributions
products.purpose: Standing procedures that make recurring support tasks consistent.
products.owner: The designated unit owner maintains procedures with staff and operators; approval follows unit policy.
products.users: Staff and teams use them for reporting, coordination, shifts and routine support.
products.when: Review before training and after approved changes or lessons learned.
products.example: Two shifts classify the same dummy outage differently. Clarify the reporting definition in the training SOP.
products.pitfall: A standing procedure is not the mission order. Verify currency instead of copying an old unit template.

products.name: Signal battle-drill / incident checklist
products.purpose: A rehearsed response aid for a defined event requiring prompt action.
products.owner: Unit leaders and technical owners define authorized actions and escalation.
products.users: Operators and staff use the trigger to coordinate a consistent response.
products.when: Rehearse in training; review after an incident or relevant change.
products.example: A synthetic shared-service outage triggers scope checks, owner notification and a dummy task retest after an approved recovery.
products.pitfall: Do not turn a generic checklist into permission to change real devices or bypass security controls.

products.name: Signal risk, assumptions and decision log
products.purpose: An editorial record of uncertainty, mission impact and decisions needed from the appropriate authority.
products.owner: Planners and technical owners supply evidence; decision and risk acceptance follow command policy.
products.users: The commander and staff use it to see what remains unresolved and what choices are needed.
products.when: Maintain through planning, rehearsal and changes.
products.example: A training service depends on an unconfirmed external provider. Record the assumption and the decision needed before rehearsal.
products.pitfall: Listing a risk does not mitigate it or mean it has been accepted.

products.name: Signal equipment and sustainment readiness tracker
products.purpose: An editorial tracker linking equipment condition and support resources to the promised service.
products.owner: Operators, team chiefs, maintenance and supply personnel coordinate with unit leadership.
products.users: Company and ESB planners use it to identify missing support and restoration blockers.
products.when: Before tasking, during preparation and as equipment condition changes.
products.example: A training team has a terminal but no verified supporting power kit. Identify the shortfall before declaring the capability ready.
products.pitfall: An inventory count is not a readiness test. This does not replace maintenance or property-accountability systems.
products.locator: Equipment transport, environmental damage and component replacement lessons

products.name: Spectrum coordination and approval tracker
products.purpose: An editorial way to track whether required spectrum coordination has been completed.
products.owner: Authorized spectrum managers coordinate applicable requests and approvals.
products.users: S6/G6 and teams need to know whether the required authorization is confirmed.
products.when: Coordinate early; confirm applicability before the training event and after changes.
products.example: A fictional training event has an unresolved coordination requirement. Mark it as a blocker and contact the authorized manager.
products.pitfall: This is not a frequency assignment, transmission authorization or spectrum request form. No actual frequencies or emitter parameters are collected.

products.name: Signal after-action review / improvement record
products.purpose: Captures what happened, why it mattered and what to improve for the next event.
products.owner: Leaders and participants compare observations with the intended training outcome.
products.users: Staff and Signal units use agreed actions to improve procedures and future preparation.
products.when: After rehearsal or execution; track actions to the next verification.
products.example: The dummy update test failed because the service owner was not included in preparation. Assign a coordination fix and test it next time.
products.pitfall: A lesson identified becomes useful when the improvement is assigned and verified. Avoid uploading real incident records.
